title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs' manuscript. Grothendieck is axiomatizing tame (moderate) topology through 'ateliers' (and 'atlas'). An atelier F is a lattice of 'figures' with two relations: ≤ (inclusion) and ≪ (roughly 'contained in the interior of' / 'well inside'). Via a multistratification M whose strata are the 'elementary figures', an atelier embeds as a sublattice F ⊂ 𝔓(M). The preceding page develops ombres (omb), nulomb, sub-atlases and 'full' sub-atlases.

On this page he crosses out a false start (a 'Corollaire 2') and returns to the theory of embeddings of ateliers, introducing a weaker notion.

Definition (quasi-embedding). A quasi-plongement f : F' → F between ateliers is a map that
(a) is monotone for both ≤ and ≪, and
(b) commutes with Sup (hence sends ∅_{F'} to ∅_F) and with Inf for ≤.
In modern terms it is a lattice homomorphism that preserves bottom and also preserves the 'way-below'-like relation ≪.

He does not require f to send elementary figures (strata) to elementary figures. When it does, f is determined by its restriction f_str1 : M' → M on strata, because every figure is a union (Sup) of strata.
- In that case f is injective if and only if f_str1 is (marginal hesitation: 'perhaps even an embedding').
- With F ⊂ 𝔓(M) and F' ⊂ 𝔓(M'), f is then identified with the direct-image map A ↦ f_str1(A) from 𝔓(M') to 𝔓(M).
- A marginal note says this is 'not clear': one would need f(F') = f_str1(F') for figures F', i.e. that the image of a figure is a union of strata. He adds 'at least when f(M') is a part of M, cf. below'.

He then proposes imposing further conditions on quasi-embeddings. The aim is that when f is injective, the induced map Ssfig(F') → Ssfig(f(F')) on sub-figures is bijective. The next page continues: in general one wants a canonical surjective order map φ : F̃ → F̃' between the posets of strata, such that the map on figures is the inverse image A ↦ φ^{-1}(A). This is essentially Birkhoff/Priestley-type duality between lattice maps and maps of underlying posets.

Purpose: to get a good category of ateliers (tame spaces) whose morphisms are compatible with stratifications.
errors: The claim that f is identified with A ↦ f_str1(A) needs f(A) = ∪ f_str1(strata of A), i.e. image of a figure is a union of images of strata. This follows from Sup-preservation only if every figure is a Sup of elementary figures (finite or arbitrary as allowed). Grothendieck himself flags this as 'pas clair' in the margin; it is a gap he defers.

Direct image does not in general commute with Inf (intersections) unless f_str1 is injective. So commuting with Inf in (b) forces strong restrictions when strata map to strata; this tension is implicit and unresolved on the page.

ideas.what: Quasi-embedding of ateliers: maps preserving ≤, ≪, Sups (incl. empty) and Infs
ideas.modern_name: bounded lattice homomorphism preserving a way-below/interior relation (morphism of 'proximity lattices' / tame-topology frames)
ideas.usually_credited_to: lattice-theoretic frameworks: Stone, Birkhoff; proximity lattices: Smyth, Jung–Sünderhauf (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; atelier formalism unpublished

ideas.what: Maps sending strata to strata are determined by the map on strata, and are injective iff that map is
ideas.modern_name: morphisms of stratified sets / Birkhoff duality for finite distributive lattices

ideas.what: Desired induced bijection on sub-figures and dual surjective poset map φ with figures pulled back (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff/Priestley duality; morphisms of stratified spaces inducing maps of strata posets

missed.claim: An axiomatic morphism notion ('quasi-plongement') for lattice-theoretic models of tame/stratified spaces. Its comparison with stratum maps is left explicitly open ('pas clair', 'il faudrait aussi imposer ... des conditions supplémentaires').
missed.quote: il faudrait aussi ... imposer aux quasi-plongements des conditions supplémentaires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It is a point-free, lattice-based approach to the morphisms of o-minimal / stratified tame topology, which is not developed in the o-minimal literature. But the content is close to standard lattice duality.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine definitional work inside the unpublished atelier formalism for tame topology. The ideas match standard lattice duality; the formalism itself is little known but the page adds no notable result.
transcription_corrections: 'Je reprends la droite des ... plongements' is likely 'Je reprends la doctrine/théorie des [crossed] plongements d'ateliers'.
The long left-margin note is roughly: 'il conviendrait de parler de "quasi-plongements" (au lieu de "plongements"), cf. plus bas'.

The partly illegible line likely reads: 'On n'exige pas qu'elle transforme fig. élémentaires en fig. élémentaires. Mais quand il en est ainsi, cette application est connue quand on connaît sa restriction'.
'(= f|fig. élém.)' and 'aux strates de multistratification'.
'il f. et s. que f_str1 le soit' (i.e. that f_str1 be injective).
The bottom-left margin is roughly: 'pas clair, parce qu'il faudrait que pour F' ∈ 𝓕', f(F') = f_str1(F'); cf. plus bas'.
